distractors.reason: 'Depend from' is a common mistake. In English, 'depend' is always followed by 'on' when we talk about something that decides a result.
We don't use 'with' after 'depend'. The preposition 'with' does not show that one thing is decided by another.
We don't say 'depend to' in English. The preposition 'to' does not fit this meaning.

example_sentence: Our picnic will ___ the weather, so bring a coat.
l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku często tłumaczą 'zależeć od' jako 'depend from', bo przyimek 'od' wydaje się pasować. W angielskim poprawnie mówimy 'depend on'.
explanation: In English, 'depend' takes the preposition 'on' when one thing is decided by another. The weather decides whether a picnic happens, so we say 'depend on the weather'.

related_collocations.example: I wait for the bus when it rains.
Look at the clouds, it may snow today.
Many people believe in good luck.

memory_tip: DEPEND ON = something decides the result (weather, time, money) | DEPEND FROM is a mistake
